item.description: Multiplex exhibition registers historic autumn milestones as Universal leads all studios worldwide; Alejandro González Iñárritu's high-stakes satire prepares global launch while Sony's 'Resident Evil' and Marvel's 'Avengers: Endgame: Encore' hold strong. Global movie theater exhibition delivered a historic commercial milestone as Universal Pictures officially crossed the monumental $5.0 billion worldwide box office threshold, becoming the very first Hollywood studio to breach the five-billion-dollar mark in calendar year 2026. The milestone was propelled by an extraordinary international slate spanning blockbuster animation, action franchises, and high-concept original features, led by Christopher Nolan's epic 'The Odyssey'—which has amassed over $1.7 billion worldwide—alongside 'The Super Mario Galaxy Movie' and musical biopic 'Michael', each surpassing one billion dollars in theatrical grosses. Simultaneously, Warner Bros. and Academy Award-winning filmmaker Alejandro González Iñárritu prepared for the high-stakes worldwide theatrical release of their R-rated satirical comedy-drama 'Digger', opening in international territories on Thursday, October 1, ahead of its wide domestic rollout on Friday, October 2. Starring Tom Cruise as a ruthless, larger-than-life oil tycoon navigating global energy geopolitics, the $160 million to $180 million production faces an intense box office test, with North American opening weekend projections tracking between $12 million and $15 million across more than 3,500 auditoriums.

In one of the most stunning final-day turnarounds in international golf history, the United States team staged a sensational Sunday singles comeback at Medinah Country Club in Illinois on September 27, 2026, defeating the International Team 17 to 13 to capture their 11th consecutive Presidents Cup victory. item.description: Revenue authority inserts Chapter-IIA into Income Tax Rules prescribing Revenue-Per-Mille benchmark of Rs195 per 1,000 views, 30% expense deduction cap, and 5% withholding on remittances; OICCI highlights Rs102.8 billion in trapped corporate tax refunds. The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) officially notified statutory regulatory orders SRO 1640(I)/2026, SRO 1641(I)/2026, and SRO 1642(I)/2026 on Thursday, September 24, 2026, enacting a dedicated legal framework for the taxation of persons earning income from remunerative social media content. Framed under Section 99C read with Section 237 of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001, the landmark amendments insert a new Chapter-IIA into the Income Tax Rules, 2002, formally incorporating resident digital content creators, online influencers, and streaming channels across YouTube, Facebook, TikTok, and Instagram into the documented tax net. Under the newly prescribed statutory mechanism, taxable income is determined by deducting allowable operational expenses from total gross remuneration, with expenses strictly capped at a statutory ceiling of 30% of total revenue. Total remuneration is legally defined as the higher of actual remuneration received (whether in cash or in kind) or the figure computed under a prescribed Revenue-Per-Mille (RPM) formula. The revenue authority established an initial benchmark RPM of Rs195 per 1,000 YouTube video views, requiring taxpayers who claim lower actual earnings to submit auditable electronic platform statements to the satisfaction of the Commissioner Inland Revenue.

item.title: Desk 01 • Statutory Directive • State Bank Liquid Reserves Touch $21.39 Billion on $3.06 Billion Eurobond Inflow as National Foreign Exchange Buffer Hits $26.79 Billion
item.description: Central bank import cover surpasses three months for first time since 2020; SRO 1495(I)/2026 amends Second Schedule rules ahead of statutory September 30 return deadline. Total liquid foreign exchange reserves held by the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) have expanded sharply to $21.389 billion, propelling the country's aggregate national foreign currency buffer—including commercial bank deposits—to an unprecedented $26.791 billion. item.description: Crisp mountain weather welcomes international cultural expeditions across Karakoram valleys; Lowari route to Chitral and Kalash valleys upgraded with eco-tourism infrastructure. item.description: Addressing Taipei tech conclave, Huang rejects calls to slow development while DeepMind and King Charles convene world AI leaders to formulate empirical safety guardrails. The Alpine Club of Pakistan, in collaboration with international mountaineering federations and local high-altitude sherpa teams, announced the successful completion of the 2026 Karakoram Ecological Restoration Campaign across K2, Broad Peak, and the Baltoro Glacier corridor. Over 14 metric tons of abandoned expedition equipment, oxygen canisters, and discarded ropes were safely retrieved and transported down to Skardu for recycling, establishing a benchmark for sustainable high-altitude tourism in Pakistan's northern sanctuaries.

item.title: Desk 06 • Premier League & Grand Slam • Arsenal Edges Chelsea 2-1 in Marquee London Derby as Manchester United Rescues 2-2 Draw at Everton
item.description: Kai Havertz and Martin Ødegaard strikes secure thrilling Emirates victory for the Gunners; Bryan Mbeumo and Benjamin Šeško headers rescue dramatic away point for Erik ten Hag's squad at Goodison Park. Sunday's Premier League fixtures delivered breathtaking drama across London and Merseyside. At the Emirates Stadium, Arsenal claimed bragging rights in the London derby with a pulsating 2-1 victory over Chelsea. After Morgan Rogers stunned the home crowd with an opening goal in the second minute for Chelsea, Kai Havertz leveled in the 25th minute with a clinical finish before Gunners captain Martin Ødegaard netted the match-winner in the 50th minute before 60,340 fans. On Merseyside, Manchester United battled back from behind to snatch an electrifying 2-2 draw against Everton at Goodison Park. Second-half goals from Bryan Mbeumo (46') and a thunderous header from Benjamin Šeško in the 88th minute rescued a vital road point after Everton had seized the lead through Harrison Armstrong and Tyrique George.
